A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LatentQA/LIT research. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical descriptions, and appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIT experiments on relational extraction, hidden personas, debiasing, sentiment control, harmful-capability elicitation, scaling, and layer selection.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds trained debiasing baselines, Gemma experiments, downstream scaling results, and qualitative steering comparisons.

M1.justification: The activation-patching decoder, three activation input types, cross-entropy training, greedy INTERPRET procedure, and gradient-based LoRA steering remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B. Gemma applies the existing method to another model; no new decoder or steering component is introduced.

E1.justification: v2 newly uses StereoSet for baseline training and adds explicit benign persona/goal steering scenarios, particularly Golden Gate Bridge behavior across unrelated prompts. Existing reading, debiasing, sentiment, and harmful-capability coverage remains. Gemma receives no visual inputs, so its inclusion does not introduce a multimodal task.

E2.justification: The retained Llama debiasing comparison expands from prompting and RepE to include trained SFT and DPO baselines, materially broadening the comparison to task-specific token-based training methods (v1 Figure 10; v2 Figure 7). v2 also evaluates training-free RepE in its new qualitative steering comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds Gemma configurations, downstream evaluation of 1B/3B Llama models, StereoSet-based SFT/DPO training, and new qualitative steering protocols. It also changes the stated easy-persona query and describes using both emphasized controls and stronger-model generation, where v1 opted for the latter. These are reported setting revisions; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds downstream persona accuracy versus model size, extending the existing loss-scaling analysis. Appendix B.1 examines transfer across model architectures, while Table 2 and Appendix D.3 add comparative case studies of unseen persona steering and fluency. The original read/write-layer sweep remains unchanged.

E5.justification: The 99% confidence intervals for relational extraction and existing error-bar reporting are retained. Moving the confidence-level description into Table 1's caption and extending the same reporting format to new debiasing rows introduce no new statistical procedure. Neither version supplies additional repeated-run or random-seed information.

E6.justification: New results include SFT/DPO Llama debiasing scores, Gemma reading accuracies of 90%/80% for easy/hard personas, and Llama 1B and 3B accuracies of 30%/12% and 96%/88%, respectively. Qualitative steering outputs are also added or replaced. Existing relational, sentiment, layer-sweep, and loss-scaling results remain unchanged. Harmful-response counts of 30/30 and 26/30 become equivalent rounded percentages of 100% and 87%.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions of activation inputs, decoder training, INTERPRET, and STEER are retained. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical derivation or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly frames the contribution around decoder fidelity and steering to unseen behaviors, while removing the introduction's specific claim of a 41% sentiment-control advantage. The central claims about open-ended activation QA, trained decoding, reading, control, and scalability persist.

C2.justification: v2 removes the limitation concerning human/model interpretation misalignment and the ethics discussion of synthetic-data bias and harmful use. It qualifies the retained hallucination concern with arguments from reading accuracy and counterfactual steering. New interpretations connect downstream scaling to usefulness, Gemma results to architectural generality, and qualitative fluency to nonlinear decoding.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix D.2's three harmful-capability control/QA specifications and 60 evaluation requests despite retaining that experiment. It also removes the explicit code/dataset/model availability statement, although the project-page link remains; actual resource withdrawal is not established. Gemma and new baseline implementation details are added, while existing LoRA settings, hardware information, and dataset-generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on refusal directions, inference-time truthfulness interventions, investigator agents, Gemma 3, and StereoSet, while removing several interpretability and risk-governance references. Positioning shifts toward expressive probes and scalable model self-understanding. Most related-work discussion and the relationships to SelfIE, Patchscopes, and visual instruction tuning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and opening motivation are substantially rewritten, the reading experiments are reordered, and sentiment evaluation moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix D.2. The discussion is sharply condensed and the ethics and reproducibility statements disappear. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: Reading/control diagrams move into the introduction, dataset illustrations move into Appendix A, and the sentiment table moves into Appendix D. The persona illustration is redrawn as a paired Turing/Shannon comparison. New scaling, Gemma, and qualitative steering tables substantially expand the displays, while earlier harmful-output examples are replaced and the harmful-response table changes from counts to percentages.

improvement.justification: The trained SFT/DPO comparisons, Gemma replication, and downstream scaling results strengthen comparative credibility and generalization evidence beyond v1's evaluations. Removing the introduction's unsupported-looking 41% sentiment advantage also improves alignment with the retained sentiment table. These gains are tempered by the loss of reproducibility details for the retained harmful-capability experiment and the narrower limitations discussion, making the overall improvement limited.
